entities.name: PMID:25450001
observations: Human whole-blood CMV cytokine-release study in 397 healthy controls; tested synthetic pp65 peptides, native CMV lysate, recombinant pp65, and nine TLR agonists with IFN-gamma and IL-2 ELISA endpoints.
Synthetic pp65 alone produced IFN-gamma of 6418 pg/mL in CMV-seropositive versus 13 pg/mL in seronegative controls; reported sensitivity and specificity were both 100%.
LTA and poly(I:C) augmented IFN-gamma responses to CMV antigens, while seronegative controls remained unaffected; numeric combination values and reproducibility metrics were not reported.
Study conclusion characterized LTA and poly(I:C) as potential costimulatory reagents, not as proven improvements in diagnostic sensitivity, specificity, or reproducibility.

entities.name: Synthetic CMV pp65
observations: Synthetic pp65 peptides elicited strong CMV-serostatus-discriminating IFN-gamma responses in whole blood; reported sensitivity and specificity were each 100% against CMV serology.

entities.name: LTA
observations: LTA augmented IFN-gamma responses to synthetic pp65, native CMV lysate, and recombinant pp65 in whole blood; the accessible report did not quantify the incremental effect or diagnostic performance.

entities.name: Poly(I:C)
observations: Poly(I:C) augmented IFN-gamma responses to synthetic pp65, native CMV lysate, and recombinant pp65 in whole blood; the accessible report did not quantify the incremental effect or diagnostic performance.

entities.name: CMV TLR assay enhancement
observations: In whole blood, LTA and poly(I:C) increased CMV-antigen-induced IFN-gamma signal, but available evidence does not establish improved sensitivity, specificity, or reproducibility over synthetic peptide alone.
